 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Reading FC midfielder Andy Rinomhota helped Zimbabwe see out a 0-0 draw against Equatorial Guinea to keep their AFCON hopes alive.
 The Warriors were held to a goalless draw by Equatorial Guinea in their first of two Group E AFCON qualifiers on November 12.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Zimbabwe's golden opportunity came in the 32nd minute when Wolverhampton Wanderers' Tawanda Chirewa broke through the opponents defence before taking a shot from inside the box which went over the bar.
 Though Rinomhota predominantly plays in midfield for the Reading, Zimbabwe coach Ramon Catala deploys him at the right-back position. A position the 29-year-old has played in previously for Cardiff and Rotherham.

 The Royals academy graduate struggled in the full-back position against Equatorial Guinea's Basilio Ndong and Santiago Eneme, who plays for Sparta Prague, and eventually picked up a yellow-card for his troubles.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Catala made a few changes after half-time, one of which saw Abubakkar Moffat replace Rinomhota in the 71st minute. Chirewa was also withdrawn and replaced by Emmanuel Jalai.
 The match was briefly interrupted by an electricity blackout in the 90th minute, with play resuming after a brief delay.
 The result leaves both Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea with four points in the group standings as both teams look to secure three points in their replay on Monday.
